title: Choose the visual world
question: The current site looks basic. Pick a replacement world for Home (category grid first). Checkout stays on eBay; Benefits stays obvious on every listing. Not a donation poster.

options.label: Specimen Binder
options.lineage: collector’s trading-card album and specimen sleeves
options.thesis: Charity Shop as a binder of object-cards: you pick a department pocket, then pull a listing whose charity lives as the affiliation stripe.
options.viewport: Desktop Home: logo as the album plate, then a strict pocket grid of category cards with a gold fringe for Benefits — no donate hero.
options.risk: Clothing shoppers may read it as collectibles-only unless apparel cards feel like lookbook specimens.

raised.raise: Signal Grid: pockets sit on a modular grid; the active pocket lights its edge like a live node.
Gold Step: Find → Browse → eBay is one numbered sequence on the binder, never a campaign.
Fringe Benefit: charity and donation sit as a narrow edge band on every card, never a poster block.
Live Index: header search is a first-class typed lane, equal in energy to the pocket grid.

options.label: Floor Directory
options.thesis: Home is a store directory: departments you already want, listed like floors, not causes.
options.viewport: Desktop Home: a large enamel directory of departments with brass index numbers; search is the you-are-here plaque.
options.risk: This is the retail-directory look most runs in this category land on.

options.label: Midnight Transit Diagram
options.lineage: metropolitan rail map as midnight-blue enamel mural
options.thesis: Categories are colored lines, charities are interchanges; you ride a department into listings.
options.viewport: Desktop Home: a diagram of departments as transit lines meeting at charity interchanges; tap a line to enter that catalog.
options.case: Holds audience identification: everyone already knows how to follow a line to a destination.
options.risk: Can read as trip-planning instead of shopping if merchandise never appears on the map.

options.label: Depot Destination Blind
options.lineage: bus-depot destination blinds in dyed duck cloth
options.thesis: Departments snap under one window like destinations; a stalled seam is the only error.
options.viewport: Desktop Home: a backlit destination blind of departments; the selected course sits in the window, others stacked above and below.
options.case: Holds product clarity: picking a destination is picking a department, with no donate story.
options.risk: Cloth-and-split-flap grammar can feel like transit hardware, not a shop, if merchandise is absent.

options.label: Man-Machine Grid
options.thesis: Departments wired on a traffic-signal grid; the live node is the category you are about to enter.
options.viewport: Desktop Home: four-across category nodes on a black-and-white grid, one hazard-red rule, connectors lighting on hover.
options.case: Loses identification: shoppers hunting Nintendo or coats do not see themselves in a man-machine band.
options.risk: Reads as an electronic-music identity, not a shop.
options.kept: Signal Grid: modular pockets and a lit active edge.

options.label: Orizuru Sequence
options.lineage: one uncut vermilion washi sheet folded into a crane
options.thesis: Shopping as thirty-two recoverable folds on one sheet, from flat geometry to a finished purchase path.
options.viewport: Desktop Home: a square sheet of numbered category folds; the active crease is gold.
options.case: Loses clarity: a 32-step fold fights the job of picking a department now.
options.risk: Vermilion paper can slide into campaign-red, which this product refused.
options.kept: Gold Step: Find → Browse → eBay as one numbered sequence.

options.label: Iridescent Cloud Edge
options.lineage: pastel diffraction bands on a forming cloud edge
options.thesis: A white catalog whose only color is a hairline fringe — Benefits as weather at the edge of the object.
options.viewport: Desktop Home: wide white field, thin category names, mint-rose-violet only at card edges.
options.case: Loses both: pastel hope reads like a donation appeal, which the brief named as wrong.
options.risk: Soft spectral color is the charity-poster mood this redesign must refuse.
options.kept: Fringe Benefit: charity lives on the card edge, never as a poster block.

options.label: Phosphor Terminal
options.thesis: The shop as one scrolling transcript: you type what you want, the catalog prints itself.
options.viewport: Desktop Home: an 80-column green catalog index; categories as typed rows, search as the cursor line.
options.case: Loses identification: general shoppers do not arrive expecting a machine-room terminal.
options.risk: Monospace-as-costume plus developer romance, against Operate’s earned familiarity.
options.kept: Live Index: search as a first-class typed lane.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished charity marketplace: logo, search, even category tiles, listing grid, charity badge — the expected shop, executed well.
canonCard.viewport: Desktop Home: centered logo, search, icon-tile departments, then featured listings with a small charity badge.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other marketplace, by design.
